items.heading: מבאר האורות הפנימיים והמקיפים דעקודים, ובו ח' ענינים: — באורות עקודים יש י"ס פנימיות וי"ס מקיפות, ומאירות בבחינת פנים וגם לצדדים ולכל סביבות א"ק
items.html: *Now from the Peh [mouth] of Adam Kadmon there emerged 1ten inner Sefirot and ten surrounding ones, and they extend from opposite 2the face down to opposite the Tabur of this Adam Kadmon. And this is the principal light, but it also shines by way of the sides to all the surroundings of this man.

*And let what we wrote above not trouble you, that 3from the light of the left Ozen [ear] that enters the Peh [mouth], the externality of the vessel was made, and from the aperture of the left Hotem [nose], the internality of the vessel was made. And although the surrounding light is greater and more excellent than the inner light, nevertheless the internality of the vessel is greater than the externality of the vessel, as is apparent to the sense of the eye. This is not so with respect to the lights, for the great light, which the vessel cannot draw and receive within it, shines from without in the secret of surrounding light, and the lesser light remains inside — which is not so with the vessels. 4And if so, how is it that from the phase of the Ozen, which is upper, the externality of the vessel should come to be, and from the Hotem, which is lower, the internality of the vessel should come to be?

items.heading: אור הפנימי מאיר בחצי עובי דופן הכלי מצד פנימי, ואוה"מ מצד החיצון, וע"י שניהם מאיר הכלי ומזדכך
items.html: The answer to this. Know that the light in its entirety is 5equal in one equality, and when it wished to enter and to be 6limited within the vessel, then 7that light which cannot enter the vessel remained outside in the phase of surrounding. And the inner light shines in the vessel from within, 8and the light passes through to half the thickness of the walls of the vessel from the side of its internality. And the surrounding light shines from outside the vessel, and passes through to half the thickness of the walls of the vessel from the side of its externality. And by means of these two lights the vessel shines and is refined.

items.heading: לפי שאו"מ גדול הרבה מאו"פ צריכה חיצוניות הכלי, שבה מתלבש או"מ, להיות זכה ומעולה יותר מפנימיות הכלי, שבה מתלבש אור פנימי
items.html: Now we require that the half of the vessel that is outside should shine on account of the surrounding light; and the surrounding light is exceedingly great, 9and its illumination would not pass over so as to be absorbed and to shine within the wall of the vessel, for there is a great distance and difference and separation between them. Therefore it was necessary 10that the internality of the vessel, which is the inferior, should become equal with the inner light, which is the inferior, and that they should shine one in the other. And likewise 20in the externality of the vessel, which is the superior, the surrounding light, which is the superior, should shine; for otherwise the externality of the vessel would have remained without illumination.

items.heading: טעם ב', אם חיצוניות הכלי לא היתה זכה לא היה אוה"מ יכול להתחבר עם אוה"פ
items.html: There is also another cause, and it is truly close to the first cause. And it is that 30the surrounding light desires and wills to join with the inner light. Therefore, if the half of the wall of the vessel 40on its outer side were not more refined, the surrounding light would not pass through it, and the inner light would be lacking the reception of the surrounding light in it. Indeed, since the half of the vessel of the outer wall is refined, the surrounding light then has the ability to pass through to the inner half of the thickness of the wall, and then they shine one in the other. And although the inner half of the wall is not refined, there is no concern in this, for the inner light passes and shines in it up to half its inner thickness, although it is not more refined.

items.heading: פנימיות הכלי יותר זכה מחיצוניות הכלי, משום שאור הפנימי מוגבל בה ומקבל הארה שלימה, משא"כ אוה"מ מאיר ברחוק בחיצוניות הכלי
items.html: And should you say that 50there is still room to object and to say: behold, by the sense of sight we see that the internality of the vessel is more refined than the externality. The answer to this is as follows: although the inner light is smaller than the surrounding light, nevertheless, 60since it is limited within the vessel, the vessel therefore receives a complete illumination from it. But the surrounding light, although it is a great light, nevertheless, since 70it is not attached and restricted with the vessel, it does not shine in the externality of the vessel as much as the inner light shines in the internality of the vessel. And with this everything comes out rightly.

items.heading: העולמות כל מה שהם תחתונים יותר, הם יותר מחוסרי השלימות עד עולם הנקודים היו ה"פ וה"מ, והשינויים היו לפי קירוב מקיפים עם הפנימיים
items.html: And know that the upper worlds, the more they are 80lower in degree one than the other, the more they are lacking in completeness one than the other. Therefore you will find that up to 90the world of Nekudim there were five phases of inner lights and five surrounding ones revealed; save that the difference between them is that in these the surrounding lights drew nearer to the inner ones, and in these they were more distant.

items.heading: מנקודים ולמטה אין יותר מה' פנימיים וב' מקיפים ופחות מזה אי אפשר להיות
items.html: And indeed, 100from the world of Nekudim downwards, which is the world of Atzilut, there was one deficiency: that there was not revealed in them, in all their particulars, more than five inner lights and two surrounding lights, which are a surrounding light for Yechida and a surrounding light for Haya. But as for the remaining three inner ones, 200there is in them no phase of surrounding lights from the phase of NRN [Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama], but only from the phase of Yechida and Haya, which surrounds them all, and not from their own phase. Indeed, there are in them yet other differences and deficiencies according to the order of the Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf] and the worlds; but the general rule concerning them is that it is impossible for there to be fewer than five inner and two upper surrounding lights.
